name: sdg06
title: SDG 6: Clean water and sanitation (SDG Atlas of Bolivia 2026)
description: The SDG 6 (Clean water and sanitation) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (SDSN Bolivia) and the 3 indicators behind it, for Bolivia's 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC), at two points in time: near the 2012 census and near the 2024 census, stored as 2012 and 2024 so that their change can be studied.

sources.title: Andersen, L. E., & Argandoña, F. (2026). Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026: Brechas y tendencias del desarrollo sostenible en las Entidades Territoriales Autónomas, 2012–2024. La Paz: Universidad Privada Boliviana, SDSN Bolivia.

geo:citation: GeoDevelopment Observatory of Bolivia (2026). SDG 6: Clean water and sanitation, from the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (343 municipalities, ~2012 and ~2024). https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geo4bolivia/blob/main/docs/datasets/sdg06.md
geo:notes: Both periods are stored at nominal years: 2012 for the Atlas's initial values (~2012) and 2024 for its final values (~2024). Each indicator's actual reference years differ (e.g. 2008 and 2023 for the health survey, three-year averages for volatile indicators) and are given in its description and in `geo:reference_years`.
Load one variable in both periods, e.g. `geo.load("sdg06", variables="index_sdg6")`, and its change with `df.pivot(index="geo_id", columns="year", values="index_sdg6")`.

The units are the 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC) of 2025. Four of them were created after the 2012 census (TIOC-Raqaypampa, San Pedro de Macha, TIOC-Jatun Ayllu Yura and TIOC-Territorio Indígena Multiétnico); the Atlas gives them values in both periods.

The indicators are rates, shares, ratios or indices, so their aggregation rule is `none`. Population-weighted averages can use the census population of the `sdg` dataset: `geo.aggregate(df, to="department", rules={"index_sdg6": "weighted_mean:population"}, weights=geo.load("sdg", variables="population"))`.

fields.name: geo_id
fields.title: Municipality ID
fields.description: GDO-Bolivia municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) of the 343-unit municipality map (SDSN Bolivia 2025: municipalities and indigenous autonomies), numbered as in GADM 4.1 plus four units created since; its boundary is in geo/boundaries/. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.

fields.name: year
fields.title: Period
fields.description: Period of the values in the row: 2012 holds the Atlas's initial values (near the 2012 census) and 2024 its final values (near the 2024 census). Each variable's actual reference years are given in its description and in geo:reference_years.

fields.name: mun_id
fields.title: INE municipality code
fields.description: Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = Nuestra Señora de La Paz), as in the Atlas. The Atlas's rows are linked to geo_id through this code.

fields.name: index_sdg6
fields.title: Clean water and sanitation index (0-100)
fields.description: SDG 6 (Clean water and sanitation) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index of SDSN, each of its 3 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst and a best value (given in each indicator's description), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped; the index is the simple mean of the available rescaled indicators. Components: Drinking-water coverage (% of population); Sanitation coverage (% of population); Wastewater treated (%). Initial value (~2012) stored at 2012 and final value (~2024) at 2024; its components refer to different years around each census. Atlas: “Índice ODS6”.
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg6_1_cap
fields.title: Drinking-water coverage (% of population)
fields.description: Percentage of the population in private dwellings with people present that has an improved drinking-water source (INE criteria, which differ for urban and rural areas). Source: INE tabulations of the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 6 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 21.4 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 98 and major challenges from 80 on. Atlas indicator 06_01_01_01_cap, “Porcentaje de la población con cobertura de agua potable” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg6_2_cas
fields.title: Sanitation coverage (% of population)
fields.description: Percentage of the population in private dwellings with people present that has improved sanitation (INE criteria, which differ for urban and rural areas). Source: INE tabulations of the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 6 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 2.7 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 95 and major challenges from 75 on. Atlas indicator 06_02_01_02_cas, “Porcentaje de la población con cobertura de saneamiento” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg6_3_tar
fields.title: Wastewater treated (%)
fields.description: Percentage of the wastewater generated that is treated in a treatment plant: volume treated divided by 80% of the drinking water billed by the municipality's water utilities (EPSA); 0 where there is no plant. Source: Water and Sanitation Regulatory Authority (AAPS), performance indicators of the regulated EPSA, 2013 and 2024. Initial value 2013 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 6 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 50 and major challenges from 15 on. Atlas indicator 06_03_01_03_tar, “Porcentaje de aguas servidas con tratamiento de aguas residuales” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
